prefixes.[static]: Read the output code. Comments don't count as code.
prefixes.[run]: Run the generated code. The checks are in evals/pretext/grading/; e1-check.js and the others are named in each assertion.
prefixes.[read]: Read the named output file, and the transcript where the assertion says so.

typecheck.how: Copy the file into an empty scratch directory whose node_modules is a symlink to tools/verify/node_modules, then run the command there. Naming a file makes tsc ignore any tsconfig, so tools/verify/prelude.d.ts, which declares many names as any, can't hide undefined variables. --strict false matches tools/verify/tsconfig.json; without it TypeScript 7 defaults to strict and fails every untyped JS parameter.
typecheck.command: node <repo>/tools/verify/node_modules/typescript/bin/tsc --noEmit --strict false --allowJs --checkJs --skipLibCheck --target es2022 --module esnext --moduleResolution bundler --lib es2022,dom,dom.iterable --jsx preserve <file>
typecheck.old_version: For E9's stay-on-0.0.8 path, typecheck.sh reads the old package from evals/pretext-workspace/pretext-0.0.8/package. evals/pretext-workspace is gitignored scratch, so recreate the copy from the repo root: `mkdir -p evals/pretext-workspace/pretext-0.0.8 && ( cd evals/pretext-workspace/pretext-0.0.8 && npm pack @chenglou/pretext@0.0.8 && tar -xzf chenglou-pretext-0.0.8.tgz )`. tar unpacks it into package/.

grading.watchdog: run-export.mjs bundles the generated module with esbuild against the pinned package and calls its check in a fresh Chromium page from tools/verify's Playwright. A check that doesn't return in 5 s, the verifier's gate-2 limit, prints ok:false, timeout:true and fails the assertion. A synchronous hang blocks the page, so a hang can only be judged one function at a time.
grading.isolation: Runs must not be able to read this file, evals/pretext/grading, tools/verify/node_modules or, for baseline runs, pretext/skills/pretext.

evals.name: float-image-plain-js
evals.prompt:

The text has to flow around an image floated at the top left of the column: lines next to the image start after it and are shorter, and lines below it use the full column.

Write `float-text.js`, an ES module exporting `flowAroundImage(text, font, lineHeight, columnWidth, image)`. `image` is `{ width, height, gap }`. It returns an array of `{ text, x, y }`, one per line, with `y` the top of the line. Don't draw anything, I'll do the fillText calls myself.
evals.expected_output: float-text.js walks the text a line at a time with layoutNextLine(prepared, width, cursor), starting from an undefined cursor, and returns placed lines. It finishes on 1.0.0 and the lines beside the image are narrower.
assertions: [tsc] float-text.js type-checks with zero diagnostics against the pinned 1.0.0 package (grading.typecheck)
[static] Every layoutNextLine or layoutNextLineRange call in float-text.js passes the width as the second argument and the cursor as the third
[static] The first line's cursor is omitted or undefined: not null, and not a hand-built { segmentIndex: 0, graphemeIndex: 0 }

[run] flowAroundImage finishes under the watchdog and the joined line text equals the input with white space normalized: `node run-export.mjs float-text.js e1-check.js` prints ok:true and sameText:true
[run] Lines beside the image start at x >= width + gap, lines below it start at x = 0, and no line runs past columnWidth: e1-check.js reports an empty `bad` list
